note: Issue 368, governor sheet A9. Placeholder prose in the default tone; the tone pass comes later. A rebel governor gives the Crown no cooperation (SPEC 12.3); the answer that moves anything is addressed to the Steward, whose duty is what makes life under the Crown worse than without it (rebel-sentiment.md section 5).

body.text: You will have had my last letter, and I said then it was my last. The hall has asked me to write one more, so I am writing it.
They would come back to the Crown on terms. The duty, first: it is {perception:burden}, and they will not pay it. After that they will talk.
I am not their envoy. I am the man with the pen. I pass it on because I would rather this ended with a letter than any other way.

options.text: and answer it as I would any other
and am not in the habit of being set terms
and will meet them further than they think

options.label: the duty will come down
options.text: The duty will come down. I have written to the Steward today. I ask nothing in return but that you read his next letter.

options.label: no terms, until they come back
options.text: The Crown does not bargain with a town in arms against it. Come back, and then write to me about the duty.
